articles.body: Asian shares were mixed Monday as volatility in technology stocks persisted, while U.S. equity futures edged higher ahead of another week of American corporate earnings results.Oil prices fell more than 2% after U.S. President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia, including on Russian energy.A sell-off of technology shares from Asia to Wall Street recently put downward pressure on stock markets, as investor concerns grow over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index was up 1.8% to 5,768.01 on Monday, after falling sharply last week. The Kospi is down more than 17% over the past month, and still well below the 9,000 mark it crossed in June at its peak on the global AI frenzy.Samsung Electronics was up 1.2%, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix added 0.4%.Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 0.6% to 64,916.70. Japanese chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron fell 2.6%, and OpenAI investor SoftBank Group dropped 2%.“We’ve been arguing for a while that volatility in tech stocks would pick up as the AI bubble continued to inflate: sharp and short-lived sell-offs were common as the ‘dotcom’ bubble inflated, for example, even as the market ultimately made very large gains on net,” Capital Economics Head of Markets for Asia Pacific Thomas Mathews wrote in a commentary Monday.Hong Kong’s stock market was closed because of a holiday. The Shanghai Composite index edged 0.4% higher to 3,730.92, after China reported better-than-expected growth of 4.5% for its economy in the July-September quarter.CXMT, China’s leading memory chipmaker, fell more than 7% despite the company forecasting a strong profit for the first nine months.Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 was 0.4% higher at 8,845.70.Taiwan’s Taiex fell 0.6%. India’s Sensex slipped 0.9%.Indonesia’s benchmark stock index fell over 5% at its peak, to its lowest level since 2020, after it plunged over 11% on Friday following a warning from index provider MSCI that it would downgrade the country from its “emerging market” status.On Friday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 declined 1.1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.3%, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite sank 2.1%.Investors this week are watching for more big corporate earnings results from the U.S., including Meta, Netflix, General Motors, Tesla and IBM. Strong company earnings have been one factor that’s been keeping U.S. stocks robust lately.As technology shares face rising uncertainties, experts say government bonds might stand to benefit as investors look for relatively safe assets, though the bond market had also been turbulent over the past few weeks.The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury eased to around 5.07% early Monday, compared with roughly 5.13% Friday. It had hit 5.35% earlier this month at its highest level since 2002, as inflation worries from the Iran war-driven energy shock and growing U.S. government debt pushed yields higher — investors demanded more in return because of the additional risks.Oil prices were down early Monday, with Brent crude, the international standard, falling 2.5% to $107.16 per barrel.Benchmark U.S. crude dropped 2.2% to $96.84 per barrel.Oil fell after Trump late Friday signed an executive order to put new broad U.S. sanctions against Russia on hold just days before they were to come into effect, drawing disappointment from Ukraine, with the move likely resulting in more energy exports from Russia.Trump's decision came not long after he said earlier this month he had reached a diesel deal with Russia in an attempt to bring down elevated U.S. fuel prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.But even with the decline, oil prices have remained elevated compared with those seen before the Iran war. articles.title: From Delhi to Gurugram: SMARR Realty’s 40-year legacy of building Delhi-NCR's retail landmarks
articles.summary: As times have gone by, there has been a change in the commercial face of the Delhi-NCR region, wherein existing retail zones in Delhi have been replaced
articles.body: As times have gone by, there has been a change in the commercial face of the Delhi-NCR region, wherein existing retail zones in Delhi have been replaced by new business and consumer zones in Gurugram. The four-decade journey of SMARR Realty has evolved within this changing scenario. With more than 3.5 million sq. ft.1 of developed space, two hotels, nine malls and a portfolio of over 350 national and international retail brands!, the company’s presence reflects the changing scale and character of the region’s growth.Its journey has been shaped not just by expansion, but by an understanding of what different locations need as their surrounding communities grow and change. SMARR Realty believes that the success of a project lies in how well it responds to the needs of its location. From retail and commercial spaces to hospitality, the company’s focus has been on understanding how businesses operate, how people use these spaces and what will keep them relevant over time. This thinking continues to shape SMARR’s approach to development and its plans for the region.“Over the years, we have seen how the needs of cities and the people living in them have changed. This has shaped the way we approach commercial real estate. Every location has its own character, and our focus has been on understanding what works for that market, whether it is retail, hospitality or a mix of commercial spaces. We want to create developments that work well for businesses, offer convenience to visitors and continue to hold value over time. As we expand across Delhi-NCR, our priority remains to build with a clear understanding of the location, backed by good planning, quality and a long-term view,” said a spokesperson for SMARR Realty.Delhi, particularly Rohini, formed an important part of SMARR Realty’s presence in the region. Crown Heights, spread across approximately 2.75 lakh sq. ft.1, reflects this mix, accommodating retail brands, offices, a car showroom and a gym. Its proximity to Rithala Metro station, along with its connection to Crowne Plaza Rohini, adds to the range of uses within the development. The company’s portfolio also includes Vikas Surya Shopping Mall, with around 2 lakh sq. ft. of retail space across four floors, and Ring Road Mall, located along the Outer Ring Road. The City Centre Rohini is another project that covers about 4 lakhs square feet1. These projects clearly show how extensive is the portfolio of SMARR Realty in Delhi on account of its location, format and commercial requirements.Besides, as Gurugram emerged as a major commercial centre within Delhi-NCR, SMARR Realty extended its presence into the city’s newer districts. In Sector 90, Sapphire Ninety covers approximately 5.5 lakh sq. ft. of built-up area, bringing together retail outlets, dining, fitness, gaming and a four-screen multiplex1. Further along this growth corridor, SMARR Vista Square in Sector 82A offers around 4 lakh sq. ft. of gross leasable area, with brands such as SPAR, Shoppers Stop, BLAAZE and Eatree, alongside Devgn Cinex1. The portfolio also includes Holiday Inn in Sector 90, with 259 rooms and suites, banquet facilities and access to adjoining retail and entertainment options. Together, these developments reflect the breadth of the company’s approach in Gurugram, where retail, hospitality and leisure have taken shape as complementary parts of its commercial presence.The next phase of SMARR Realty’s growth is taking shape in New Gurugram, where ongoing developments in Sectors 89 and 92 are set to add to the region’s expanding commercial infrastructure. The company’s projects include Vista Corner, Vista Centre and Vista Avenue in Sector 89, along with City Centre 92 in Sector 92. Planned across a mix of retail, restaurants, entertainment and office spaces, these developments are expected to cater to a wider range of business and consumer needs, with anchor stores adding to their commercial mix. Vista Avenue is also planned to feature a 252-key Le Méridien hotel, while City Centre 92 has a proposed 48,000 sq. ft. D-Mart hypermarket. Together, these projects mark the next stage of the company’s expansion across Delhi-NCR.Thus, from Delhi’s established retail centres to Gurugram’s newer commercial corridors, SMARR Realty’s four-decade journey reflects the changing nature of business and urban life across the region. Its portfolio spans retail, commercial and hospitality developments, with the next phase of growth taking shape in New Gurugram. articles.title: 'Geography is real': Rubio says India-US trade deal close, explains Trump admin's stance on Russian oil
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Monday said that India and the US are close to finalising a trade deal.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Monday said that India and the US are close to finalising a trade deal. He also explained the reason behind Washington's consideration of India energy needs before imposing sanctions or tariffs linked to Russian oil.Speaking to reporters in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, Rubio said the US had waived some sanctions in recent months to limit their impact on global energy supplies and prices."We've had to waive sanctions over the past few months because of the impact on global supplies and prices...We have to manage all of these things.”Explaining how Washington was balancing trade negotiations with India and decisions on sanctions, Rubio said countries had to consider several factors when making foreign policy decisions, including how easily they could access alternative energy sources.“We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that. That's one of the things we taken into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers and things of that nature. Every country has a complex set of factors that it has to take into account. Geography is real. For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources. That's not an excuse, but all of that has to be balanced when making foreign policy..."Rubio is currently in Uzbekistan and is scheduled to visit Mumbai on Tuesday to meet external affairs minister S Jaishankar. He will also travel to Jamnagar later in the week, which is home to one of the world's largest refineries.Why the US is taking another look at Russian oil sanctionsRubio's remarks come after US President Donald Trump waived several sanctions related to Russian fuel sales that were due to take effect under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.The law, which has now been paused, would have allowed the US to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods imported from the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas. India and China are among these countries.Rubio said the proposed measures would affect not just Russia but also countries that buy its energy. The US wants to use a 60-day period to study how the sanctions and tariffs could affect the global economy and its own economy."These sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countries—India, for example, and others. And so I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy," Rubio said.He said India had diversified its energy sources but still bought a significant amount of energy from Russia. Switching to other suppliers immediately was not easy, he added."You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next. But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States. So we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is," he added.Graham bill and geopoliticsRubio also said the US was considering changes in the global situation since the Graham bill was passed. He pointed to the growing conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi militia, along with the war between Russia and Ukraine.He said global energy supplies were under pressure because of several factors, including Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and damage to energy infrastructure during the Russia-Ukraine war."I think when the bill was passed, one of the reasons the waivers were put in there is understanding that they would need some period of time to study this, given all the different things that are that are going on in the world right now, including the pressure on global energy supplies that are happening not just because of Iran and not just because of the Straits of Hormuz, but increasingly because of the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia, and because of the war with Ukraine and Russia, where energy infrastructure is being hit, and so that's having an impact on global prices as well," he said.Meanwhile, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal last week said that the first part of the agreement had been finalised and had moved to the legal drafting stage. "US bilateral trade agreement's first tranche has been finalised and it is going through final contours, the legal drafting and we hope to be able to finalise that soon and operationalise that once we get the competitive advantage over our peer countries," Goyal said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Renting a house in UP? Proposed Rs 1,000 stamp duty on Rs 2 lakh annual rent aims to cut costs, boost registered rent agreements and protect tenants and landlords, here’s how
articles.summary: Recently, the Uttar Pradesh government announced plans to revamp the state's tenancy rules, including changes to the stamp duty and registration charges
articles.body: Recently, the Uttar Pradesh government announced plans to revamp the state's tenancy rules, including changes to the stamp duty and registration charges that are applicable to rental agreements.At a press conference, Ravindra Jaiswal, Minister of State for Stamp and Registration Fees, said the state government was considering a stamp duty of Rs 1,000 on rent agreements where the annual rent amounts to Rs 2 lakh.What is the current trend?Under Indian law, residential rent agreements covering a period of 11 months do not require compulsory registration, according to an ET report. This is one reason why 11-month agreements are so common.One drawback of verbal or unregistered rental arrangements is the difficulty of establishing proof. Such agreements generally cannot be relied upon as evidence unless a court permits their use.Circle rates are another factor behind the widespread practice of keeping residential tenancy agreements unregistered.Also Read | Homebuyers paid Rs 2.06 crore but got no flat, builder said payments meant accepting delay; Bombay HC orders interest payout from 2017 saying RERA allows for unconditional right to monthly interestHow could the proposed UP rent law benefit tenants and landlords?The proposed changes could offer practical advantages to both tenants and property owners, particularly by making it easier and less expensive to register rental agreements.Legal experts expect the proposed changes to complement the Uttar Pradesh Urban Premises Tenancy Regulation Act, 2021.Malav Virani, Partner at MDP Legal, told ETthat the government's primary concern was the low rate of registration of rent agreements across the state.Under the existing system, stamp duty and registration charges for tenancy agreements were calculated as a proportion of the rent, at roughly 4%, based on four times the property's circle rate.Virani explained that this formula could result in a substantial stamp duty burden even when the rent agreed upon was relatively modest.To avoid these expenses, many landlords and tenants opted for verbal arrangements rather than entering into written agreements. Even when they prepared written documents, they often left them unregistered.Also Read | She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additionsAccording to Virani, the reforms are intended to make the Act easier to implement by addressing the cost of registering tenancy agreements, which has discouraged people from doing so. Another objective is to reduce landlord-tenant disputes reaching the courts because the parties lack properly documented agreements or rely on informal arrangements.Virani said the lower stamp duty and registration costs would provide relief to tenants and encourage them to formalise their rental arrangements. Registering an agreement would also help tenants secure the protections available under the Act.Virani says: “Armed with a registered agreement, tenants will enjoy a strong legal standing with proof of tenure, agreed rent, and other terms being documented.” Such records could prove important if a landlord tries to evict a tenant unlawfully, challenges the agreed rent or denies that a tenancy arrangement exists.Having a properly registered agreement is intended to strengthen the legal position of both parties and discourage practices that violate their contractual rights.Landlords, too, stand to benefit because the terms of the tenancy would be recorded in writing and formally registered.According to Virani, this documentation can help protect property owners if a tenant refuses to leave after the agreement expires, defaults on rent payments or commits similar breaches of the tenancy terms.Also Read | He bought a home, gave it for redevelopment years later and sold new flat for Rs 1.95 crore within 8 days; taxman denied LTCG exemption and added Rs 80.14 lakh, but ITAT grants reliefYou use AI every day. articles.title: Stock market crash today: Sensex ends over 870 points down, Nifty50 below 22,900 - top reasons for fall
articles.summary: Stock market crash today: After a week of rallying, the Indian equity benchmarks crashed in trade on Monday.
articles.body: Stock market crash today: After a week of rallying, the Indian equity benchmarks crashed in trade on Monday. Heavy selling in major private banking stocks, along with other factors, weighed on investor sentiment and pulled the benchmark indices into negative territory.Nifty50 ended the day at 22,888.95, down 257 points or 1.11%. BSE Sensex closed at 73,852.90, down 876 points or 1.17%. The decline provisionally erased nearly Rs 4.70 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies, taking it down to Rs 467 lakh crore.V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited said, “The momentum created by the 2.8% surge in Nifty last week and the good results from the banking majors after the better-than-expected results from the leading IT companies have the potential to keep the market resilient. However, the escalation of the tensions in Hormuz and the consequent surge in Brent crude to $109 will act as a strong headwind to the market.”“Even though the attractive valuations of the large-caps and the appreciation of the rupee have turned the stance of FIIs towards India a bit positive, it is unlikely to sustain, given the high crude price. Large-caps outperforming the mid-and small-caps is a rational trend, and this is likely to sustain, going forward. The market actions this week are likely to be stock-specific in response to the Q2 results,” he added.Axis Bank was the biggest loser on the Sensex, with its shares falling around 5%. HDFC Bank, Infosys, Trent, HUL, Bajaj Finserv, NTPC, Bajaj Finance and ICICI Bank also declined by up to 2%. Adani Ports and Maruti Suzuki moved against the broader trend, gaining as much as 2%.Selling pressure extended to the broader market as well.Why did stock market crash today?Banking stocks downShares of major private sector lenders, particularly Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, led the losses on the benchmark indices after their second-quarter results failed to meet market expectations.Axis Bank shares dropped more than 5% after the lender reported a 38% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore for the second quarter of FY27. Despite the growth in earnings, the result fell short of analysts' estimates.HDFC Bank also faced selling pressure, with its shares declining more than 2%. The country's largest private sector lender reported a net profit of Rs 19,510 crore for Q2FY27, up 4.6% from Rs 18,641 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.Shares of ICICI Bank and Yes Bank also came under pressure, falling by more than 1% each.Foreign investor outflows continue to weigh on sentimentForeign institutional investors (FIIs) bought Indian equities worth Rs 1,166 crore on Friday, according to provisional data from the NSE. However, the purchase was relatively small compared with the substantial outflows recorded during October.FIIs have been net sellers in nine of the 11 trading sessions so far this month, keeping sustained pressure on the domestic equity market.Crude oil prices highBrent crude futures fell by more than 2%, but continued to trade well above last week's levels at over $107 per barrel. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was hovering close to $100 per barrel.The decline in oil prices followed US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia, including restrictions targeting its energy sector. However, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump would take up to 60 days to evaluate the economic consequences of the waiver.Weakness across global marketsIndian equities followed the broader decline across several international markets. Japan's Nikkei slipped 0.64%, while Indonesia's Jakarta Composite plunged more than 5%. South Korea's Kospi moved in the opposite direction, rising around 2% as investors bought AI stocks after their recent decline.Indian equities are seen as having an anti-AI advantage. As a result, gains in AI-related stocks can sometimes coincide with weakness in the domestic market.US markets also suffered a sharp sell-off on Friday. The technology-heavy Nasdaq tumbled more than 2%, while the S&P 500 declined by over 1%.Investors book profits after recent gainsMonday's decline came after Indian markets had rallied sharply over the previous two trading sessions. The Nifty gained more than 2% on Thursday and Friday despite several headwinds, prompting investors to lock in some of their recent profits.Market participants were also bracing for possible volatility around the Nifty's expiry ahead of Tuesday's market holiday.Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited said, “Indian equities came under renewed selling pressure, reversing the recent recovery as weak global cues and selling in private banks and IT stocks weighed on investor sentiment. Global markets remained cautious ahead of a busy week of corporate earnings. Private banks remained under pressure following quarterly earnings and concerns over margin trends, while PSU banks bucked the broader weakness, supported by expectations of relatively resilient margins and asset quality.”“Crude oil prices eased after the US waived key sanctions linked to Russia, raising expectations of increased Russian fuel supplies to the global market. articles.title: Home repair costs jump 76% in a decade
articles.summary: Home improvement costs have jumped 76% since 2015 as homeowners stay put to avoid high mortgage rates.
articles.body:
Home improvement and repair costs have escalated in price in the last decade, adding to the strain of tight budgets for Americans, a new analysis finds.

The median cost of a home improvement project has risen 76.1% from 2015 to 2025, from $1,200 to an inflation-adjusted $2,113, according to a LendingTree analysis.

"Home improvement costs are increasing so much in part because the price of most anything is going up. The cost of labor and building is likely playing a big role," Matt Schulz, LendingTree chief consumer finance analyst, told USA TODAY.

Homeowners are making repairs, not moving

Homeowners are staying in their homes longer rather than moving and with that come repairs and upgrades, said Schulz.

"Plenty of families feel stuck because they have a house that doesn't meet their current needs but a mortgage rate that is far lower than what they'd get today. They simply can't bring themselves to trade their 3% rate for a 7% rate, so they're staying put. That isn't likely to change anytime soon, unfortunately," he said.

Routine maintenance on owner-occupied homes is an estimated $1,433 a year on average, but that amount rises to $1,706 annually for homes built before 1940. New properties are the cheapest to maintain, with costs falling to three figures for homes built in 2015 and later, LendingTree said. Houses built from 2022 to 2023 cost $173 on average to maintain.

Sixty-four percent of the projects analyzed were completed by a professional, with the median project costing an estimated $4,103. That's compared to $845 spent on a DIY project.

LendingTree analyzed U.S. Census Bureau American Housing Survey and U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data for its analysis.

What types of projects are homeowners taking on?

Nearly 6 in 10 owner-occupied homes, or 51.6 million of the nation's 86.9 million owner-occupied properties, underwent some type of improvement during the research's two-year lookback window. There were 139.9 million individual projects, or an average of 2.7 projects per improved home.

But the most common project wasn't a big renovation. The most common single project category was a combined group covering water heaters, dishwashers and garbage disposals, with homeowners adding or replacing appliances in 11.7% of all projects tracked. The median cost was $845.

Schulz said it doesn't surprise him that maintenance and repairs account for the biggest projects.

"Home improvements may be bigger and flashier, but ongoing maintenance and repairs are more common. Most any homeowner can tell you that they just never seem to stop," he said. "They might only cost a few hundred dollars rather than the several thousand dollars people may spend on larger renovations, but they happen so regularly that it can add up to a major financial burden for families."

articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista: "Los trabajadores de entre 55 y 57 años están hartos y quieren jubilarse, pero no es posible"
articles.standfirst: El economista toca un segmento de población que empieza a pensar en la jubilación
articles.summary: El economista toca un segmento de población que empieza a pensar en la jubilación
articles.body: El economista Gonzalo Bernardos se ha metido de lleno también en materia laboral. Y lo ha hecho concretamente con un sector de la población activa que son los trabajadores de entre 55 y 57 años. Muchos trabajadores quieren dejar de trabajar antes de los 60 años, pero todavía no cumplen los requisitos para acceder a una pensión. Por ello, el analista económico mete el dedo en la llaga: "Hay personas de entre 55 y 57 años que están hartas de trabajar y quieren jubilarse, pero no es posible", señalaba Bernardos en declaraciones recogidas por 'Business Insider España'. Porque se trata de un perfil de trabajadores que acumulan ya un largo camino laboral, pero aún deben esperar varios años para acceder a la jubilación ordinaria. La jubilación ha ido cambiando los últimos años y a partir de 2027 vuelve a suceder. La edad ordinaria de jubilación será de 67 años para quienes no hayan cotizado al menos 38 años y seis meses. Lo que alcancen ese periodo podrán jubilarse a los 65 años. Por ese motivo, contar ya con muchos años cotizados no permite retirarse automáticamente a los 55 o 57 años. El envejecimiento de la población provoca que haya un aumento de presión al sistema público de pensiones. La jubilación de la generación del 'baby boom' aumenta el número de personas que empiezan a cobrar una prestación, mientras que la evolución del empleo y de las cotizaciones resulta clave para financiar los pagos. "Nos vamos acercando a 2040 y no hay más remedio que jubilarse más tarde", detalla el economista.

articles.title: Homebuyers are canceling sales at near-record rates
articles.summary: Nationwide, 14.5% of homes fell out of contract in September.
articles.body:
Homebuyers are backing out of contracts at near-record rates, a potential sign of how higher mortgage rates are prompting buyers to rethink their plans.

Nationwide, 14.5% of homes fell out of contract in September, according to Redfin data, the highest share on record apart from the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Homes can fall out of contract for a number of reasons, such as inspection findings or financing pitfalls, or when a buyer just has a change of heart. But pending sales tend to fall through at higher rates when buyers have more options and more negotiating power, as they currently do in much of the country.

Indeed, metro areas that are notably buyer's markets, like Jacksonville and Tampa, Fla., and Las Vegas, all had contract cancellation rates approaching 20%, higher than anywhere else in the country. But they're relatively rare in strong seller's markets like San Francisco, where just 2.8% of deals fell apart.

Claire Boston is a Senior Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: A big 'yikes' still hangs over the AI trade as Meta and Tesla report: What to watch this week
articles.summary: Tech earnings are back in action this week with reports from SpaceX, Tesla, and Meta.
articles.body:
Move over Wall Street, because it's tech's time to shine.

After a busy first proper week of earnings that saw a relatively mixed picture out of the big banks, attention turns to the tech trade, where Meta ( META ), SpaceX ( SPCX ), and Tesla ( TSLA ) will all report results. With little economic data coming ahead of the Federal Reserve's late October meeting, the first batch of tech results will have our undivided attention.

After a relatively quiet Monday, the week's major earnings get properly underway on Tuesday with SpaceX and Netflix ( NFLX ), where co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters are likely to face questions (scrutiny or praise, we'll see) over recent layoff announcements. Wednesday will see results from Tesla and Meta, set to provide an early read on the state of the Magnificent Seven and the AI trade writ large.

Several of the so-called "prime" defense contractors — Northrop Grumman ( NOC ), Lockheed Martin ( LMT ), and RTX Corp. ( RTX ) — will also post their quarterly results, joined throughout the week by industrial heavyweight Honeywell ( HON ) and energy giant NextEra ( NEE ).

The quiet economic calendar will feature a smattering of housing and labor market data ahead of Friday's consumer sentiment readings from the University of Michigan, which are likely to capture the most attention.

When Meta reports third quarter earnings on Wednesday, Mark Zuckerberg and the company's other executives are likely to take myriad questions around one topic: the company's growing push into AI.

The focus for Meta recently has, of course, been the launch of Muse Spark, a personal AI agent product that set off waves of bulls claiming agentic workflows will revolutionize whole industries and of bears claiming, basically, "No one wants this."

The product immediately racked up millions of downloads, reaching the 5 million mark faster than OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT, Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude, and SpaceX's Grok.

The product launch — one of Meta's largest announcements in years — has put the company " back on offense with AI, " argue Bank of America analysts Justin Post and Nitin Bansal, who have a Buy rating on the stock with an $810 price target.

"We think Muse and Model traction can drive multiple expansion with stock at 22x 2027 EPS," the analysts wrote.

There are some risks for Meta, Post and Bansal said. Muse downloads and activity could slow down, and Google could release a competitor consumer agent product that would take market share away from Meta.

articles.title: Albertsons begins its $8 billion trial against Kroger over failed merger
articles.summary: By Tom Hals WILMINGTON, DEL., Oct 19 (Reuters) - US grocery chain Albertsons Companies will begin making its case in court on Monday for more than $8 billion...
articles.body:
WILMINGTON, DEL., Oct 19 (Reuters) - US grocery chain Albertsons Companies will begin making its case in court on Monday for more than $8 billion in damages against larger rival Kroger for allegedly sinking their agreed $24.6 billion merger two years ago.

Idaho-based Albertsons, ‌whose chains include Safeway, Acme and Kings Food Markets, claims that Kroger broke its commitment to obtain regulatory approval for the deal ‌by refusing to sell a sufficient number of stores. As a result, Albertsons said it is owed a premium of up to $6.88 billion the deal would have delivered to its shareholders, ​as well as the $600 million termination fee and more than $1 billion in tax adjustments.

The bench trial is scheduled to run two weeks in Delaware's Court of Chancery in front of Vice Chancellor Lori Will. Rulings often take months after the trial ends and the outcome can be appealed to the Delaware Supreme Court.

The 2022 merger was meant to position the two companies and their 5,000 stores to better compete with newer entrants into grocery markets such as Walmart, Costco, Amazon ‌and Aldi.

However, combining the largest and second-largest US grocers ⁠was challenged by states and the administration of Democratic President Joe Biden, which argued the deal would remove direct competition and lead to higher prices at checkout.

In December 2024, federal and state courts blocked the deal and Albertsons immediately terminated ⁠the merger, which Ohio-based Kroger said cut off its ability to appeal.

Since the termination, Kroger's stock has risen about 4% and Albertsons has lost nearly 30%, both lagging the S&P 500 index, which rose by more than a quarter.

The trial comes a week after Albertsons unveiled a cost-cutting review of its business and after Kroger, which ​owns ​the Dillons, Ralphs and Fred Meyer chains, planned to cut 3,000 jobs and invest in ​technology to lower prices.

Albertsons said that Kroger violated what it ‌claimed was an obligation to take "any and all actions" to get antitrust approval, up to selling 650 stores.

Albertsons described in court papers the various divestiture packages that Kroger offered regulators as an attempt to minimize what it had to sell to protect the profitability of the post-merger business, rather than to get regulatory clearance.

It said Kroger created a $400 million executive bonus pool to encourage senior managers to take a highly aggressive approach to demands from regulators.

Kroger said in its court papers Albertsons was misreading the merger agreement and said that it kept its obligations, pinning the deal failure on regulatory opposition. It ‌said that the Biden administration wanted it to sell more than 650 stores and ​courts blocked the merger because they took a narrow view of the grocery market by ​excluding Amazon, Costco and others.

articles.title: Global freight costs surge 130% as Middle East tensions continue to rattle shipping routes: Report
articles.summary: Global container freight rates have climbed 130% since February 2026, with renewed tensions in the Middle East driving up shipping costs.
articles.body: Global container freight rates have climbed 130% since February 2026, with renewed tensions in the Middle East driving up shipping costs. India's container-based export-import trade, however, continues to expand, according to a Jefferies report.The surge marks a reversal after a prolonged period of easing freight rates. Shipping costs had declined through much of 2025 and early 2026 as the demand-supply balance improved following elevated rates in 2024. Rates have since risen sharply, moving from around $2,000–2,500 in February 2026 to approximately $4,000–4,500 in October.The report noted, "Freight rates have risen 130 per cent since Feb-26, due to the impact of Middle-East tensions." It also identified the possibility of shipping lines resuming transit through the Suez Canal as a key factor to watch, stating, "The potential impact of shipping lines' return to the Suez Canal, despite Middle East tensions, is a key monitorable."The latest increase in freight costs comes against the backdrop of growth in India's containerisable trade. The value of the country's container-based exports and imports rose 23% year-on-year in September 2026, according to Jefferies. Exports increased 22% during the month, while imports grew 23%.Trade performance varied across destinations. India's exports to the United States registered a 48% year-on-year increase in September. In contrast, shipments to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia fell 12-15% compared with the same month last year.The report's accompanying data traces the movement in global container freight rates from their highs in 2021-22. Rates subsequently dropped substantially before recovering in 2024, followed by another decline through much of 2025 and the early part of 2026. The recent upswing has reversed that trend.Port activity across India also showed mixed movement in September. Cargo volumes at major ports rose 13% year-on-year, while non-major ports recorded a 1% decline.Within the non-major port segment, Gujarat registered a 3% increase in volumes compared with September 2025. Ports in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu reported growth of 6-7%. However, major and non-major ports along India's eastern coast witnessed a sharp fall in volumes during the month, the report said.Jefferies flagged the possible return of shipping lines to the Suez Canal, despite ongoing tensions in the Middle East, as an important development for the global freight market. Any changes in shipping routes could influence freight rates, keeping the region's developments in focus for businesses reliant on international cargo movement.While freight costs have risen alongside growth in India's containerisable trade, the figures cited in the report do not establish that the increase in shipping rates has already affected the country's export-import growth.You use AI every day. articles.title: Netflix faces questions on user engagement ahead of third-quarter report
articles.summary: Oct 19 (Reuters) - Netflix investors are expecting details on how the streaming giant plans to sustain growth when it reports third-quarter results on Tuesda...
articles.body:
Oct 19 (Reuters) - Netflix investors are expecting details on how the streaming giant plans to sustain growth when it reports third-quarter results on ‌Tuesday, as competition intensifies and user engagement shows signs of fatigue.

Ted Sarandos, ‌the co-CEO of Netflix, recently admitted the company "is not growing as fast as I want us to", ​and suggested live programming could be an opportunity to accelerate growth.

The streamer is contending with a fundamental shift in entertainment as lower-cost, creator-led videos chip away at premium scripted content. YouTube, the dominant streaming platform in the US, has nearly double the ‌viewing time of Netflix and ⁠continues to gain market share, according to Nielsen.

• Netflix is expected to post its slowest third-quarter revenue growth ⁠in three years, with sales forecast to increase 11.8% to $12.87 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

• It cut about 6% of its workforce in a move that analyst ​Ross Benes ​of Emarketer said reflected the streaming industry's ​shift to profitability.

• Netflix also ‌saw a change in its content leadership, with longtime head of content Bela Bajaria leaving the company and former Disney executive Peter Rice taking over.

• Its US user churn rose 16.6% year-over-year in the third quarter, roughly double the pace of the prior three quarters, while downloads in the US and Canada fell 20%, according ‌to market research firm Apptopia.

• Jefferies estimates average ​monthly viewing time per Netflix member fell to ​49 hours in the first ​half of this year from 66 hours in the first half ‌of 2023.

• The 2026 FIFA World ​Cup and a weaker ​content slate than last year weighed on Netflix's engagement, analysts said.

• The company recently acquired broadcast rights to air the 2030 FIFA World Cup ​in Spain and Andorra.

• Netflix ‌is betting on advertising to diversify revenue, with Jefferies forecasting ad revenue ​to reach $7.5 billion in 2029.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; ​Editing by Edmund Lee and Devika Syamnath)

articles.title: Elon Musk says he will give a SpaceX share to ‘every kid in America’
articles.summary: Elon Musk has said he will give every child in America a stake in SpaceX, his $2 trillion aerospace and artificial intelligence company, as tech firms face intensifying scrutiny over their impact on society.
articles.body: Elon Musk has said he will give every child in America a stake in SpaceX, his $2 trillion aerospace and artificial intelligence company, as tech firms face intensifying scrutiny over their impact on society. “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” he wrote on X on Monday. “This will be the first of many.” SpaceX only began trading publicly in June (and had the biggest initial public offering in history). The company’s shares were trading for about $146 when the market closed on Friday. Musk’s proposal was thin on detail. It is not clear how those shares would be distributed to the tens of millions of American children or whether all of them would even be eligible. According to the United States Census Bureau, there are roughly 73 million people under the age of 18, making Musk’s potential giveaway worth about $10.7 billion at SpaceX’s current share price. Offering young people a stake in the US stock market isn’t a new idea. This month, the Treasury Department automatically signed up millions of under-18s to Trump Accounts, a new federal savings and investment vehicle, with children born between the start of 2025 and the end of 2028 eligible for a one-off $1,000 government contribution. Damage control? Musk’s offer came in response to Anthropic’s announcement on Sunday that it will commit at least 5% of its shares — worth $48 billion at the private company’s latest valuation — to a “Public Benefit Fund” that will donate money to social causes. The fund could make “large donations” to non-profit organizations or “direct distributions to specific populations,” the company wrote on its website, adding that the money could help mitigate the impact of artificial intelligence on people’s jobs. Musk retorted on X: “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public… This is what I will be doing.” Both offers come as AI companies face intense backlash over the safety of their products (Anthropic itself recently warned of the “existential risk to humanity” posed by the technology), the potential for AI to push humans out of their jobs en masse, as well as the social and environmental impact of the industry’s gargantuan data center build-out. Tech titans more broadly are catching heat. New movies like “The Social Reckoning” — about a Facebook employee blowing the whistle on unsafe company practices — and documentary “You Can See Everything” — following blood testing start-up founder and convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes — are helping to remind audiences of the long-running recklessness of some in Big Tech. Musk himself is the subject of the new documentary “Musk,” charting his life and career. It is unsparing in its criticism of some of his business practices and controversial foray into politics.

articles.title: Man sold his house and bought a Rs 1.10 crore flat jointly with wife; income tax department denies Rs 55.48 lakh capital gains exemption for half the amount, but ITAT Mumbai gives full relief
articles.summary: You sell a property and reinvest the money you get from the sale in another property, and claim capital gains exemption in your income tax return.
articles.body: You sell a property and reinvest the money you get from the sale in another property, and claim capital gains exemption in your income tax return. The catch however is that the property you buy as a replacement is jointly owned by you and your wife.And the Income Tax Department disallows a part of the exemption claim because of that. What do you do? In one such case the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Mumbai has provided relief.What the case is aboutA man sold his residential property and invested the proceeds in another flat in Mumbai. The replacement property was jointly registered in his and his wife's names, with the total investment of around Rs 1.10 crore. He claimed exemption on the capital gains under Section 54 of the Income Tax Act.He filed his income tax return for assessment year 2013-14 on October 10, 2013, declaring an income of Rs 3,72,770. After scrutiny, the Assessing Officer assessed his income at Rs 59,21,730, with the partial disallowance of his Section 54 claim being a key reason for the increase.Also Read | Man worked in South Korea and received salary in US dollars in NRE account, income tax department sent notice; ITAT Bangalore sets aside assessment and orders fresh reviewWhilst the taxpayer claimed the full tax exemption towards the entire gains under the aegis of Section 54 which simply requires reinvestment of gains in a new home, the tax authorities denied the partial deduction attributable to the wife's share in the new flat.The Assessing Officer restricted the deduction by approximately Rs 55 lakh, corresponding to the wife's 50% share in the new property. The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) upheld this decision, holding that the replacement property needed to be purchased in the taxpayer's name and that joint ownership did not qualify for the full deduction.Why did ITAT rule in the man’s favour?The man challenged the decision before ITAT. He argued that the investment had come from the proceeds of his original property and that his wife's name had been included for convenience. His grounds of appeal also referred to his wife's ill health and his intention to give her mental peace.To support his claim, he submitted a gift deed dated May 19, 2012, bank statements, account summaries, purchase documents and income tax returns. He also relied on the fact that he had reported the entire property in his own return.Also Read | Farmer sold fruits and vegetables at APMC, deposited cash in bank account, but faced notice for unexplained large deposits; ITAT Bangalore gives relief, accepts land records and sale bills as proofThe tribunal first considered the Bombay High Court's ruling in CIT v. Dr Laxmichand Narpal Nagda. That judgment had explained that legal title being transferred within a specified period was not necessarily a precondition for Section 54 relief. It observed that “holding of a legal title within a period of one year is not a condition precedent for attracting section 54.”The ITAT also distinguished Prakash v. ITO, the decision relied on by the tax authorities. In that case, the replacement property had been acquired entirely in the name of the taxpayer's adopted son, effectively giving up the taxpayer's rights over it. This case was different, the tribunal said, because his wife was a joint owner and he had not given up his rights over the property.The tribunal observed: “although the property agreement bears the name of the assessee's wife as co-owner, in our view, this by itself cannot disqualify the assessee from seeking deduction under Section 54 of the Act.”Another part of the reasoning concerned Sections 27 and 64 of the Income Tax Act. These provisions address circumstances in which property ownership or income from assets transferred to a spouse is attributed to the transferor for tax purposes. The tribunal reasoned that the wife's name on the property could not, by itself, bar the Section 54 claim.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemptionAmit Gupta, Partner at Saraf and Partners sees this as a signification judgment which is premised on the underlying ethos of the investment-based tax deductions under the Income tax Act.Provisions of Section 54 of the Income tax Act 1961 which represents a ‘house for a house’ based exemption is available with respect to reinvestment of long-term capital gains arising from transfer of residential property into purchase/construction of another residential property within the ascribed timeframe.According to Gupta, the judgment clearly relays that the substance of the transaction has to be looked into especially from the fund flow/reinvestment perspective which assumes great importance in the Indian context wherein families often add a spouse's name for various reasons, viz. succession planning, reducing stamp duty incidence, convenience or comfort.Also Read | Grandmother and her son gifted 2.5-acre land to his second wife, who sold it; his daughter from first marriage claimed it was ancestral, but Madras HC rejects her pleaHe lists the reason for the judgement going in the man’s favour:•⁠ ⁠The taxpayer demonstrated (though gift deed and bank statements) that the money contributed by the wife towards her share in the new flat was gifted by him to his wife and thus her payment towards the flat was really his investment.•⁠ ⁠Interesting analogy was also drawn from the clubbing provisions enshrined in the ITA which are in nature of anti-abuse provisions seeking to curb the mischief wherein Assessee’s seek to divest themselves of title to their assets/income in favour of their family members(viz. spouse, minor child) for nil/inadequate consideration in order to avoid payment of taxes on incomes.•⁠ ⁠The Clubbing provisions(Section 64(1)(iv) of the ITA) deems for the purpose of taxation, that income from asset transferred by the transferor assessee for inadequate consideration to their spouse to continue to be income of the transferor assessee.•⁠ ⁠Correspondingly, even for the purposes of Income from House property, the provisions of the ITA(Section 27) deem the transferor to be the owner where a house property is transferred to a spouse otherwise than for adequate consideration, ensuring the rent is taxed on the transferor notwithstanding title.On such an analogy the Tribunal observed, merely because the name of the wife is included in the property, the same solely cannot lead to denial of claiming under Section 54 of the ITA.•⁠ ⁠Further, the Tribunal placed reliance on various favourable judicial precedents which held that the benefit of Section 54 cannot be denied merely because the name of the wife/son was included in the new property. Also, the Tribunal distinguished other case relied on by the tax authorities on the underlying factual matrix and averred that the wife is neither a stranger nor an unconnected person to the assessee and thus purchase of property in the name of the wife is permissible since the taxpayer had neither given up his domain/right over the new property nor created any third party rights in the new flat.“The judgement underscores the importance of maintaining proper comprehensive documentation to corroborate overall arrangements, i.e., the tax filings and the funding/contributions should align and reflect the underlying position demonstrating contribution towards the property acquisition,” he says.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claimYou use AI every day. articles.title: So you say you hate ‘surveillance pricing’
articles.summary: Local governments are banning “surveillance prices,” or when companies use personal data to set prices. But broad actions could hinder any possible benefits.
articles.body: “Surveillance pricing” sounds very, very bad. Consumers think that companies are tracking their search history, location and income to charge more for groceries and other purchases. Naturally, lawmakers are trying to crack down on this supposed nightmare. In Colorado, the legislature passed a bill this summer to ban companies from using customers’ personal data to set individualized prices. The concern is that two people could be charged different amounts for milk based on what the data spits out about their willingness to pay. But Colorado Gov. Jared Polis saw a big problem with the bill. “Many Coloradans won’t get discounts on items they buy if I were to sign this,” Polis said in a June letter. “It would punish differentially lower prices, not just higher prices.” He vetoed it. Americans are channeling their rage over high prices, AI and giant companies gathering their data into the issue of “surveillance pricing.” A growing number of cities and states are responding with legislation to reel in companies’ use of customers’ personal data to set prices, especially at large grocery stores and fast-food chains. Some bans also target electronic shelf labels at stores. Unions have backed these restrictions on electronic labels because they fear the technology will eliminate the need for workers to change thousands of paper tags in stores each week. But the tech is more neutral, and Polis’ veto exposed a contradiction with the growing backlash to the practice: the same algorithm that companies use to charge more also can deliver lower prices, reduce food waste and create other benefits for consumers. Broad state and local bans cut off the possibility of lower prices and other tech that delivers benefits, economists, attorneys and marketing experts say. “Some of the surveillance pricing laws are not only unlikely to protect consumers, they may even harm them,” said Jean-Pierre Dubé, a marketing professor at the University of Chicago’s Booth School of Business. Evidence also shows that neither “surveillance pricing” nor electronic shelf labels increase overall prices. “There is essentially no change in pricing behavior after these digital labels are installed,” a study tracking more than 180 million price records at grocery stores last year found. Dynamic pricing on steroids The debate around “surveillance prices” often blurs two different practices: dynamic pricing, which adjusts prices based on supply and demand and other market conditions, and personalized pricing. Dynamic pricing has existed for decades. Happy hour, lunch specials and end-of-season clearance sales are familiar examples. Consumers also encounter dynamic pricing when they buy plane tickets online or order Uber rides. There is little evidence that dynamic pricing raises prices overall. In some industries, including airlines and restaurants, it has actually enabled companies to offer lower prices. Airlines have long used dynamic pricing to offer lower fares to travelers who are flexible on their travel dates or willing to fly at off-peak hours. A large restaurant chain that used an algorithm to adjust food delivery prices found that it helped smooth out orders throughout the day, according to a 2023 Harvard University study. The algorithms slashed prices during slow hours to attract customers who would otherwise dine elsewhere, bringing the average price down across the day. Lower prices weren’t the only benefits of dynamic prices. In the grocery industry, research from the University of San Diego in 2023 found that dynamically pricing perishables cuts down food waste by 21%. But as AI has expanded companies’ ability to personalize prices across more industries, the practice has gradually been described in more nefarious terms such as “AI surveillance pricing” and “price discrimination.” Economic populists such as Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders blame “surveillance pricing” for driving up prices, claiming AI will make things worse. Lindsey Owens, the CEO of progressive economic think tank Groundwork Collaborative, gained traction for her warnings about the opaque ways corporations use customers’ personal data to rip them off. Owens pointed to a patent Walmart received in 2023 for technology that can remotely deploy dynamic price changes to electronic shelf tags: “If a customer has tuna fish, they may be offered a different price for mayonnaise,” the patent says. Facing public uproar, Walmart last month defended its practices and told customers: “We don’t set different prices based on who you are or the time of day.” Walmart has little incentive to abandon its business strategy of stable, consistent prices, said Ioannis Stamatopoulos, a professor of operations at the University of Texas at Austin who has studied dynamic pricing. The company relies on a model known as everyday low prices — rather than sales and coupons — to draw shoppers. Rapid price fluctuations would alienate Walmart’s customers, Stamatopoulos said. “They would rather keep you happy and coming back instead of risking your continued business for a few opportunistic cents,” he said.

articles.title: India-New Zealand FTA to take effect from Oct 20; target to double trade to $7bn by 2030
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Free Trade Agreement between India and New Zealand will be enforced on Tuesday (October 20), allowing duty-free access to Indian goods
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Free Trade Agreement between India and New Zealand will be enforced on Tuesday (October 20), allowing duty-free access to Indian goods across Wellington’s entire market.The announcement comes from a ministry of commerce and industry presentation, cited by ANI.Labour-intensive sectors such as textiles, apparel, leather and footwear are expected to benefit from the removal of tariffs of up to 10 per cent from the agreement’s implementation. Other sectors, including engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, machinery, chemicals and agricultural products, are also expected to gain better market access.The agreement provides New Zealand market access across 70 per cent of tariff lines, while India has excluded the remaining 30 per cent. For New Zealand, duties on 30 per cent of the tariff lines covered under the agreement will be eliminated immediately. The remaining lines will see phased reductions over a period of up to 10 years, tariff cuts or tariff-rate quotas. ANI reported.India gets 100 per cent duty-free access for its goods exports to New ZealandCommerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal had previously announced that the deal could be operationalised in the latter half of October."We are expecting that the agreement will get operationalised in the latter half of October 2026. The exact date for the same will be announced soon ... because both sides have to completely take stock of the operationalisation processes and procedures," he said on September 15Double trade by 2030Under the India-New Zealand Strategic Partnership Roadmap, the two countries have set a target of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to NZD 7 billion, equivalent to around Rs 35,000 crore, by 2030.According to the New Zealand ministry of foreign affairs and trade, India-New Zealand two-way trade totalled nearly NZ$3.95 billion in the year ended December 2025. New Zealand exported NZ$2.03 billion worth of goods and services to India during the period, making India its 21st-largest goods export market and fifth-largest services export market.Key exports to India included travel services worth NZ$1.14 billion, forestry products worth NZ$399 million, horticulture products worth NZ$114 million, including apples worth NZ$81 million and kiwifruit worth NZ$33 million, aluminium worth NZ$86 million, iron and steel worth NZ$80 million, and wool worth NZ$77 million.According to the ministry of commerce and industry, New Zealand is India’s second-largest trading partner in Oceania. India’s services exports to New Zealand grew by 13 per cent in 2024 to reach US$634 million, with travel, IT and business services among the major sectors. India-New Zealand merchandise trade also rose from US$855 million in 2015-16 to US$1.298 billion in 2024-25.Over the 10-year period, India’s exports to New Zealand increased by 130 per cent, while imports rose by 7.21 per cent. New Zealand has also committed to invest USD 20 billion in India over 15 years.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Why Intel stock just got a big upgrade
articles.summary: Intel catches some love.
articles.body:
After a sweeping tech stock sell-off last week, Wall Street is on the hunt for bargains.

And JPMorgan ( JPM ) may have found one in chip giant Intel ( INTC ), with the stock off about 36% from the June highs. Analyst Harlan Sur upgraded his rating on Intel to Neutral from Underweight on Monday.

Intel stock rose 4% in premarket trading.

Here are several of Sur's thoughts that stood out:

CEO is driving fundamental change: "More importantly, since Lip Bu Tan's appointment to CEO, we believe the team's execution and competitiveness in their core client/datacenter compute market has improved, the team's execution on next-gen manufacturing has significantly improved (yields, manufacturability, foundry process/design rule compatibility, advanced packaging) and the team has several initiatives (ASICs) which exploit INTC's strong IP portfolio, SOC design capabilities, and leading edge internal manufacturing capabilities."

Estimates could be poised for lift-off: "Despite near-term concerns on AI infrastructure spending sustainability, we believe increasing agentic AI workloads (CPU intensive) and a very tight supply chain for leading edge silicon should drive continued positive EPS revisions in the upcoming earnings season and through CY27 (our CY28 EPS estimates are ~15% above consensus)."

articles.title: 'One SpaceX share for every kid in America': Can Elon Musk actually do it?
articles.summary: Elon Musk has said he will give every child in America one share of SpaceX in 2027.
articles.body: Elon Musk has said he will give every child in America one share of SpaceX in 2027. While the statement itself seems inchoate, it also raises questions about whether the ambitious promise can be fulfilled.The SpaceX CEO said the move would be the first of many such initiatives. However, turning the announcement into reality could prove complicated, given SpaceX's status as a privately held company and the legal and practical challenges of distributing shares to millions of children.How many shares would Musk need?"Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Musk said in his announcement on his own platform, X.However, if Musk means every child under 18 living in the United States, the country has roughly 73 million children, based on recent US population estimates. This means he would have to distribute around 73 million shares, although the final number would depend on the eligibility criteria.There are two broad ways this could happen.Musk could transfer shares he already owns to eligible children.SpaceX could issue additional shares as part of a new arrangement.The two options would have different implications for the company and its existing shareholders.The scale of the exercise would also raise questions about eligibility.It is not yet clear whether the promise would cover every person under 18, only US citizens, or children who meet other conditions. Those details would be essential to determining the number of shares required.SpaceX is not a publicly traded companyAnother key hurdle is that SpaceX is privately held, unlike companies whose shares are traded on a stock exchange. This means its shares cannot be bought and sold as freely as those of a publicly listed company.A private company's shares may also be subject to restrictions on transfers. Musk could therefore face limits on how he distributes his holdings, depending on SpaceX's corporate rules and the terms governing its shares. Any large-scale transfer would need to account for those conditions.Valuing the shares could also be more complicated than it would be for a listed company. SpaceX does not have a continuously updated stock-market price that anyone can use to determine the value of a share at a given moment. The value assigned to the shares would depend on the company's valuation and the terms of the proposed distribution.The legal and practical hurdlesGiving shares to millions of children would involve more than transferring ownership. The plan would need to comply with applicable securities laws and SpaceX's corporate rules. The company may also need to address how such a large number of new shareholders would affect its ownership structure and administrative arrangements.The recipients' ages would add another layer of complexity.Since many beneficiaries would be minors, arrangements may be needed for adults or custodians to hold or manage their shares until the children are legally able to do so. The process would also require a reliable way to establish who qualifies, verify their details and transfer the shares to the right recipients.Tax implications could be another consideration for both the person making the gift and those receiving it.The treatment would depend on the structure of the giveaway and the rules that apply. With millions of potential recipients, even routine administrative steps could become a substantial undertaking.Musk's hint at plan to deliver SpaceX share promise\Elon Musk's response to Anthropic's announcement of committing the company's funds for public benefit does give a potential clue as to how he plans to fulfil his promise.Musk had suggested that he would distribute company shares directly to the public, rather than through a separate fund.He made the remarks in response to Anthropic's announcement to initially commit 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, with the stake potentially increasing as the company's valuation rises."I recommend giving the shares directly to the public," Musk wrote on X, "This is what I will be doing."Musk's comments suggest that he favours direct distribution over an intermediary fund. But giving a SpaceX share to millions of children would still involve significant legal and logistical hurdles.Is Musk's promise feasible?The idea is not necessarily impossible. A transfer of existing shares or a specially structured distribution could, in principle, provide a way to give children an ownership stake in SpaceX. But the scale of the proposal makes its execution far more complicated than an ordinary gift.There are various factors yet unannounced by Musk or SpaceX that would determine how the promise of US children having shares in the company plays out. It includes:Who would qualify.How the shares would be distributed.Whether the company's rules permit the transfers.How ownership by minors would be handled.For now, Musk's statement sets out a promise rather than a confirmed distribution plan. Until the eligibility rules, legal arrangements and method of transfer are made clear, it remains uncertain how the proposed giveaway would work in practice.You use AI every day. articles.title: Cleveland-Cliffs Shares Rise Over 7% as Third-Quarter Earnings Exceed Expectations
articles.summary: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. (NYSE:CLF) reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings above analyst expectations on Monday, supported by higher steel prices and inc...
articles.body:
Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. (NYSE:CLF) reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings above analyst expectations on Monday, supported by higher steel prices and increased revenue compared with the previous year.

Shares in the US steel producer rose more than 7% in premarket trading following the publication of its financial results.

The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.28, compared with analysts' consensus estimate of $0.22. Revenue reached $5.6 billion, slightly below market expectations of $5.71 billion.

Cleveland-Cliffs also reported adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of $612 million, exceeding the $575 million guidance issued three months earlier.

Third-Quarter Revenue Increases 18% Year on Year

Cleveland-Cliffs generated third-quarter revenue of $5.6 billion, representing an 18% increase from the $4.7 billion reported in the corresponding period of 2025.

The company shipped 4.2 million net tonnes of steel during the quarter, with an average selling price of $1,177 per net tonne.

This compared with an average selling price of $1,032 per net tonne in the third quarter of 2025, representing an increase of approximately 14%.

The higher average selling price contributed to the year-on-year increase in revenue.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $612 million, exceeding the company's previous quarterly forecast by $37 million.

The results also reflected changes in sales volumes and unit production costs compared with the second quarter.

Cleveland-Cliffs Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Lourenco Goncalves said the company's third-quarter performance exceeded the guidance provided earlier in the year.

"Third quarter was our strongest quarter in three years, with adjusted EBITDA of $612 million, a number above the $575 million guidance we provided three months ago," Goncalves said.

"Average selling price, sales volumes, and unit costs all moved in the right direction relative to Q2 performance."

The company's financial results indicate that higher steel selling prices contributed to the improvement in quarterly earnings.

Management also identified changes in shipment volumes and unit costs as factors affecting performance relative to the preceding quarter.

Fourth-Quarter EBITDA Forecast at Approximately $715 Million

Cleveland-Cliffs expects adjusted EBITDA of approximately $715 million for the fourth quarter of 2026.

The forecast represents an increase of approximately $103 million from the third-quarter result of $612 million.

articles.title: Meta's AI vision doesn't come cheap, and its earnings could prove it
articles.summary: Bringing Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's AI vision to life doesn't come cheap.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) has enjoyed a wave of favorable headlines with its new products over the past month, but bullish Wall Street may be reminded of one thing when the company reports earnings on Wednesday.

Bringing CEO Mark Zuckerberg's AI vision to life doesn't come cheap.

"Our overall take is that Meta will qualitatively guide to capex and total expense levels that are above the Street, and hence we believe it is probable that Meta's Street [earnings] estimates for 2027 come down," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney warned. "Our uneducated guess is that management will guide for total expense growth in 2027 at a somewhat slower percentage growth rate than in 2026," or about 40% year over year, and capital expenditures dollar growth "similar to 2026," or around $70 billon.

How the Street would interpret an even more aggressive spending tone by Meta is murky. For one, the stock has rallied a solid 6% in the past month amid a barrage of new product drops .

Meta officially launched its newest frontier AI systems, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full , in the past week. The models are engineered specifically for multistep reasoning, coding, and autonomous personal agent workflows.

They are the first new models from Meta's new Superintelligence Labs. So far, they are receiving high praise for their speeds compared to the likes of OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 and Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude Opus 5.5, spurring optimism about Meta's ability to compete for big enterprise business in the AI boom.

Meanwhile, the Muse AI agent — released in September — appears to be off to a strong adoption start .

The argument could be made that the Street is overlooking Meta's cost of building out AI, given that the stock has rallied steadily. On the other hand, the Street could embrace higher spending to support the growth of praised products.

All in, it's a confusing setup on the stock heading into the earnings report.

"We continue to view Meta as a core name to own as the AI Revolution moves from models to agents, because a frontier model paired with 3.6 billion daily users is a combination few competitors can match," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.
